headnotes.la: etc. Non dicit: In principio dicit Deus, Fiat coelum et terra. Sed dixit
headnotes.en: etc. He does not say: In the beginning God says, Let heaven and earth be made. But he said

headnotes.la: quoniam universaliter nomine coeli et terrae comprehendendum erat quidquid fecit Deus, deinde per partes explicandum quomodo fecit. Unde sequitur
headnotes.en: because under the name of heaven and earth there was to be comprehended universally whatsoever God made, and thereafter it was to be set forth part by part how he made it. Whence there follows

headnotes.la: id est, per verbum suum fecit. Vel quia cum primum fiebat informis materia spiritualis, vel corporalis, non erat dicendum
headnotes.en: that is, by his Word he made it. Or because, when formless matter, spiritual or corporeal, was first coming to be, it was not to be said

headnotes.la: incongruum enim erat a Deo dici,
quia formam verbi non imitatur imperfectio, nisi cum generis sui conversione ad creatorem sit perfecta creatura; ut cum dicitur
headnotes.en: should be said by God, since imperfection does not imitate the form of the Word, save when, by the conversion of its own kind to the Creator, the creature is made perfect; so that when it is said

headnotes.la: intelligamus eum ad se imperfectionem creaturae revocare. Cum ergo dicitur
headnotes.en: we may understand that he calls back to himself the imperfection of the creature. When therefore it is said

headnotes.la: commemoratio Filii fit, quia principium est; sed cum dicitur
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Gen. 1:1 *creavit*, "created"] there is a commemoration of the Son, because he is the beginning; but when it is said

headnotes.la: … aeternaliter significat exstitisse. Et quem in conditionis initio coelum et terram creasse narrat, tanta celeritate operationis omnipotentem esse declarat, cui voluisse, facere est. Bene ergo dicitur
headnotes.en: … it relates to have created heaven and earth at the outset of the founding, it declares to be omnipotent by so great a swiftness of working, for whom to have willed is to do. Well therefore is it said

headnotes.la: etc. Utrumque scilicet, simul, quamvis utrumque simul ab homine non dicatur. Unde propheta terram in initio factam ostendit dicens, psal. CI
headnotes.en: etc. Both, that is, at once, although both are not uttered at once by a man. Whence the prophet shows the earth to have been made in the beginning, saying, psal. CI

headnotes.la: etc. Coelum non visibile firmamentum, sed empyreum, id est, igneum vel intellectuale, quod non ab ardore, sed a splendore dicitur, quod statim repletum est angelis. Unde in Job XXXVIII
headnotes.en: …ible firmament, but the empyrean, that is, the fiery or intellectual heaven, which is so called not from burning but from splendour, and which was straightway filled with angels. Whence in Job XXXVIII

headnotes.en: [n: (BEDA in Gen., tom. II, col. 191.)] Scripture says

headnotes.en: …art from the world's revolving, as soon as it was created was filled with holy angels: whom the Lord testifies to have been founded in the beginning together with heaven and earth, saying, Job XXXVIII

headnotes.la: …; sive spiritualem vitam ante conversionis formam quasi fluitantem. Spiritus Dei superferebatur, quia subjacebat bonae voluntati Creatoris, quod formandum et perficiendum inchoaverat. Dictum est etiam
headnotes.en: …re floating, before the form of its conversion. The Spirit of God was borne above, because that which he had begun to be formed and perfected lay beneath the good will of the Creator. It is also said,

headnotes.la: … animantis. Intelligimus ergo non de spiritu mundi dici, ut putant multi; sed de Spiritu sancto, qui et ipse est omnium vivificator: si autem vivificator, et conditor; si conditor, et Deus. Psal. CIII
headnotes.en: …s not said of the spirit of the world, as many suppose; but of the Holy Spirit, who is himself the quickener of all things: and if the quickener, also the founder; if the founder, also God. Psal. CIII

headnotes.la: etc. In quo subsistentes requiesceremus flatu ejus vivificati, et unda baptismi abluti
headnotes.en: etc. In whom, subsisting, we might rest, quickened by his breath and washed by the wave of baptism

headnotes.en: …earthly Jerusalem is figured, which is in the tribe of Benjamin: whose people afflict their mother with grievous sorrow by shedding the blood of the prophets, and by crying out for the death of Christ
[var: Vulg. Gen. 35:18 *Egrediente autem anima prae dolore*, "and her soul departing for pain"] [n: (HIERON.)] Since indeed she was dying,

headnotes.la: …populus Israel figuratur: qui thorum concubinae polluit, id est legem Veteris Testamenti praevaricando maculavit. Quod autem concubina Vetus Testamentum significaverit, Paulus ostendit dicens, Gal. IV
headnotes.en: …rael is figured: who defiled the couch of the concubine, that is, stained the law of the Old Testament by transgressing. And that the concubine signified the Old Testament, Paul shows, saying, Gal. IV

headnotes.la: Sciendum quod non omnes reges commemorat qui fuerunt antequam haberent reges filii Ismael, quorum primus Saul, sed hos omnes tantum qui regnaverunt antequam moreretur Moses
headnotes.en: It is to be known that he does not record all the kings who were before the children of Ismael had kings, of whom the first was Saul, but only all those who reigned before Moses died

headnotes.la: …s ex duodecim filiis Jacob, prae caeteris patri dilectus, Christum significavit, quem Deus Pater secundum carnem natum caeteris fratribus ex Abrahae stirpe progenitis praetulit. Unde amabat eum Jacob,
headnotes.en: …loved of his father beyond the rest, signified Christ, whom, born according to the flesh, God the Father preferred to the rest of the brethren begotten of the stock of Abraham. Whence Jacob loved him,

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (ISID.)] Jacob mittit filium ut de fratribus curam gereret; et Deus Pater Filium unigenitum, ut genus humanum peccatis languidum visitaret. Unde Galat. capite quarto
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (ISID.)] Jacob sends his son to take care of his brethren; and God the Father his only-begotten Son, to visit the human race sick with sins. Whence Galatians, chapter four

headnotes.la: Missus est Joseph ut videret si cuncta prospera essent erga oves: et Christus ait Matthaei decimo quinto
headnotes.en: …cati*; the chapter cited, Gal. 4:4, has *Misit Deus Filium suum, factum ex muliere*] Joseph was sent to see whether all things were prosperous with the sheep: and Christ says, in Matthew the fifteenth

headnotes.la: *Defectionem.* In grandi enim defectione erant, qui de fratricidio cogitabant
headnotes.en: *A falling away.* For they were in a great falling away, who were thinking of fratricide

headnotes.la: …triarchae, Christum significat, qui descendit ab baptismum Joannis. Hiras enim interpretatur *videns Deum:* Odollamites, *testimonium in aqua,* quia Joannes videns Christum venientem ad baptismum, ait
headnotes.en: …s Christ, who went down from the baptism [sic: *ab baptismum*] of John. For Hiras is interpreted *seeing God:* Odollamite, *testimony in water,* because John, seeing Christ coming to the baptism, said

headnotes.la: [n: (STRAB.)] *Allegorice.* Venit Dominus ad oves tondendas, id est peccatis exonerandas, de quibus dicitur
headnotes.en: [n: (STRAB.)] *Allegorically.* The Lord came to shear the sheep, that is, to unburden them of their sins, of which it is said

headnotes.la: …edens cum hoc habitu ad portam Enaiim , quod interpretatur *fons:* quia currebat velut cervus ad fontes aquarum, pervenire ad semen Abrahae. Illo non cognoscente fecundatur, secundum illud Psalmi XVII
headnotes.en: …ch is interpreted *a fountain:* because she was running like a hart to the fountains of waters, to come to the seed of Abraham. She is made fruitful, he not knowing it, according to that of Psalm XVII

headnotes.la: Accepit in occulto annulum, monile, et virgam, quia vocatione signatur, justificatione decoratur, glorificatione exaltatur
headnotes.en: She received in secret the ring, the necklace, and the staff, because she is sealed by vocation, adorned by justification, exalted by glorification

headnotes.la: Sermo Hebraicus, Enaiim, transfertur in *oculos.* Non est igitur nomen loci, et est sensus,
headnotes.en: The Hebrew word Enaiim is rendered *eyes.* It is not therefore the name of a place, and the sense is,

headnotes.la: Mittitur promissus haedus tanquam meretrici, id est exprobratio peccati, per Odolamitem, tanquam increpantem,
headnotes.en: The promised kid is sent as to a harlot, that is, the reproach of sin, by the Odollamite, as by one rebuking,

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (HIERON.)] « Cognovit autem Judas, etc. In Hebraeo habetur
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (HIERON.)] « And Judas acknowledged, etc. In the Hebrew it is found

headnotes.la: …exit, et nascendo praecessit, significavit quod Israel in opere legis manum extenderet, et prophetarum et ipsius Christi cruore pollutam contraheret: populus vero gentium postea prorumperet, ut essent
headnotes.en: …etch out his hand in the work of the law, and would draw it back defiled with the blood of the prophets and of Christ himself: but that the people of the Gentiles would afterwards break forth, so that

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (AUG. in Gen.)] Ad ordinem tendit Scriptura unde recesserat, ut illa narret quae supra gesta sunt
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (AUG. in Gen.)] Scripture returns to the order from which it had departed, that it may relate those things which were done above

headnotes.la: [n: (AUG. Quaest. in Gen.)] Ubi in Latinis codicibus
headnotes.en: [n: (AUG. Quaest. in Gen.)] Where in the Latin copies is written

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (AUG. Q. in Gen.)] Tertio, nisi fallor, insinuatur nobis in hoc libro Spiritus sanctus. Primo ubi dictum est supra [n: (cap. I)]
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (AUG. Q. in Gen.)] For the third time, unless I am mistaken, the Holy Spirit is intimated to us in this book. First where it was said above [n: (cap. I)]

headnotes.la: secundo ubi dicit Deus supra [n: (cap. VI)]
headnotes.en: secondly where God says above [n: (cap. VI)]

headnotes.la: …super universam terram Aegypti: et Dominus noster, postquam distractus est a Juda, sicut Joseph a fratribus et de inferni carcere surrexit, ascendit currum coelestis regni, de quo dicitur psalmo LXVII
headnotes.en: …nd of Egypt: and our Lord, after he was sold away by Juda, as Joseph by his brethren, and rose from the prison of hell, ascended the chariot of the heavenly kingdom, of which it is said in psalm LXVII

headnotes.la: et accepit potestatem praedicandi et judicandi a Patre. Unde Phil. II
headnotes.en: and he received from the Father the power of preaching and of judging. Whence Phil. II

headnotes.la: … byssina, id est, carne sancta bysso splendidiore, et stola immortalitatis. Accepit quoque torquem auream, id est, intellectum bonum. Praeco antecedit eum, id est, Joannes Baptista, qui ait Matth. III
headnotes.en: … shining than fine linen, and with the robe of immortality. He received also a golden collar, that is, a good understanding. A herald goes before him, that is, John the Baptist, who says in Matth. III

headnotes.la: etc. Joseph de carcere eductus, super Aegyptum constituitur; et Christus resurgens accepit
headnotes.en: etc. Joseph, brought out of the prison, is set over Egypt; and Christ rising again received

headnotes.la: … mundus. Joseph interpretatur *augmentatio* sive *ampliatio:* sed in illo Joseph ampliationem non habuit nisi sola Aegyptus; in nostro vero, universus mundus. Ille erogavit triticum; noster Dei verbum
headnotes.en: … world had perished. Joseph is interpreted *increase* or *enlargement:* but in that Joseph none had the enlargement save Egypt alone; in ours, the whole world. He dispensed wheat; ours the word of God

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (ISID. in Gen., tom. V.)] Est frumentum in Aegypto: dicit et Deus Pater, Osee XI
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (ISID. in Gen., tom. V.)] There is corn in Egypt: God the Father says also, Osee XI

headnotes.la: etc., nec tamen obtinuit. At Judas dicens
headnotes.en: etc., and yet he did not prevail. But Judas, saying

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (AUG.)] Mendacium videtur, sed aliquid significare credendum est. Argentum enim, quod datur et non minuitur, quod et probatum appellatum est, illud forte est de quo dicitur psalmo XI
headnotes.en: …)] It seems a lie, but it must be believed to signify something. For the silver, which is given and is not diminished, which also has been called tried, is perhaps that of which it is said in psalm XI

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (AUG.)] Solent ebriosi hoc testimonium adhibere sibi in patrocinium propter Joseph, qui valde sapiens commendatur. Sed hoc verbum pro saturitate ponitur in Scripturis, unde psalmo LXIV
headnotes.en: …G.)] Drunkards are wont to bring forward this testimony in their own defence, because of Joseph, who is commended as very wise. But this word is put in the Scriptures for fulness, whence in psalm LXIV

headnotes.en: etc. [n: (AUG. Quaest. in Gen., tom. III.)] What is it that according to other copies is read thus

headnotes.la: Hoc enim non usquequaque consonat, etc., *usque ad*
headnotes.en: For this does not agree in every point, etc., *as far as*

headnotes.la: etc. Trecenti argentei dantur Benjamin, quos a Christo accepit qui praedicat Trinitatem, vel Christi crucem. Unde Paulus ait I ad Corinth. II
headnotes.en: etc. Three hundred pieces of silver are given to Benjamin, which he received from Christ who preaches the Trinity, or the cross of Christ. Whence Paul says in the first to the Corinthians, II

headnotes.la: …ium sensuum. Praecellit ergo Paulus abundantia meritorum: sed et fratres, id est alii praedicatores, habent gratiam suam, id est binas stolas, ut confiteantur Christum Deum et hominem. Unde Prov. XXXI
headnotes.en: … in the abundance of his merits: but his brethren also, that is, the other preachers, have their own grace, that is, two robes apiece, that they may confess Christ to be God and man. Whence Prov. XXXI

headnotes.la: …, sed secundum electionem gratiae, et imponat manum super oculos ejus, et caecitatem auferat; quod distulit, ut postremus crederet, qui ante non putavit esse credendum. Unde ad Romanos undecimo capite
headnotes.en: …ay his hand upon his eyes, and take away his blindness; which he deferred, that he should believe last who before did not think that it was to be believed. Whence to the Romans in the eleventh chapter

headnotes.la: …: animas enim dictas pro hominibus, a parte totum figurata locutione, nullus ambigit. Sed quomodo ipsam partem, id est animam cujus nomine totus homo significatus est, alienamus ab eo quod dictum est,
headnotes.en: …figurative manner of speech naming the whole from a part, no one doubts. But how we are to alienate that very part, that is, the soul by whose name the whole man is signified, from that which is said,

headnotes.la: …bens eis cibaria, quia fames terram oppresserat: sic et Dominus parentibus, id est patriarchis et prophetis, ex quibus est secundum carnem, sive omnibus sanctis, de quibus in Evangelio dicit Matth. II
headnotes.en: … had oppressed the land: so also the Lord, to his kindred, that is, to the patriarchs and prophets, of whom he is according to the flesh, or to all the saints, of whom he says in the Gospel, Matth. II

headnotes.la: his dat terram optimam, de qua dicitur psal. XXVI
headnotes.en: …ater, et soror, et mater est*, "Whosoever shall do the will of my Father, who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother."] to these he gives the best land, of which it is said, psal. XXVI

headnotes.la: etc. Quaeritur, eum Joseph frumenta colligeret, unde homines viverent, pecora unde vivebant, cum tanta fames invaluisset, et fratres Joseph Pharaoni dixerunt
headnotes.en: etc. It is asked, since Joseph was gathering the corn whereby men might live, whence the cattle were living, when so great a famine had grown strong, and the brethren of Joseph said to Pharao

headnotes.la: … qui in spiritali Aegypto sunt et ejus opes ambiunt, servos esse. Nullus est enim liber Aegyptius, qui carnalis est, et venundatus sub peccato: Pharao enim eos subjecit; unde fortasse dicitur Exod. XX
headnotes.en: …s that all who are in the spiritual Egypt and court her riches are slaves. For no Egyptian is free, who is carnal, and sold under sin: for Pharao made them subject; whence perhaps it is said, Exod. XX
[var: Vulg. Ex 20:2 *qui eduxi te de terra Aegypti*, "who brought thee out of the land of Egypt."] Whence Rom. VI
etc. And in the same place

headnotes.la: …s est iniqua, cum amans terrena despicit coelestia, et propter avaritiam se subjicit diabolo. Dei autem permissio est justa, cum eum qui spernens meliora, elegit pejora, dimittit arbitrio suo ut cadat
headnotes.en: …he heavenly, and for covetousness subjects itself to the devil. But God's permission is just, when he leaves to his own choice, that he may fall, the man who, despising better things, has chosen worse

headnotes.la: etc. Allegorice emptio Joseph, qui frugibus emit terram Aegypti, significat Christum doctrina et sanguinis pretio redimere mundum. Quod autem dicit
headnotes.en: etc. Allegorically the purchase of Joseph, who bought the land of Egypt with corn, signifies that Christ redeems the world by doctrine and by the price of his blood. And as to what he says

headnotes.la: …s possessoribus permittuntur, quia actualis vitae usus unicuique conceditur, ut seminet virtutum opera, et fructus justitiae metat in vitam aeternam, qui a Christo nobis tribuitur. Unde Joseph dicitur
headnotes.en: …use of the active life is granted to every one, that he may sow the works of the virtues and reap the fruit of justice unto life eternal, which is bestowed on us by Christ. Whence it is said to Joseph

headnotes.la: [n: (AUG., ubi supra. )] Quod habent Latini codices,
headnotes.en: [n: (AUG., ubi supra. )] That which the Latin codices have,

headnotes.la: Hoc etiam in loco quidam frustra simulant adorasse Jacob summitatem sceptri Joseph: quod scilicet honorans filium potestatem illius adoraverit, cum in Hebraeo multo aliter legatur
headnotes.en: In this place also certain men vainly pretend that Jacob adored the top of Joseph's sceptre: namely, that honouring his son he adored his power, whereas in the Hebrew it is read far otherwise

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (Isid. in Gen., tom. V.)] Sicut factum est in Esau et Jacob, dicente Domino
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (Isid. in Gen., tom. V.)] As was done in Esau and Jacob, the Lord saying

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (HIERON., ubi supra. )] Quia Juda *confessio* vel *laus* interpretatur, etc., *usque ad* juxta eumdem sensum aliis verbis Ecclesia monstratur, de qua dicitur Matth. V
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (HIERON., ubi supra. )] Because Juda is interpreted *confession* or *praise*, etc., *as far as* in other words the Church is shown according to the same sense, of which it is said, Matth. V

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (ISID.)] Vel catulus leonis in somno requievit, quia non necessitate, sed potestate. Unde
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (ISID.)] Or, the lion's whelp rested in sleep, because not of necessity but of power. Whence

…o tollit eam a me : sed ego pono eam a meipso, et potestatem habeo ponendi eam*, "No man taketh it away from me: but I lay it down of myself, and I have power to lay it down."] But as to what he adds,

headnotes.la: etc. Nullus, subaudi, nisi ipse qui ait Joan. II
headnotes.en: etc. None, understand, save he himself who says, Joan. II

headnotes.la: etc. Gentes quas sibi subjunxit. Unde Ezech. XVIII
headnotes.en: etc. The Gentiles whom he joined to himself. Whence Ezech. XVIII

headnotes.la: id est doctrina legis, quae carnalem populum vel parvulum lacte alebat: sed
headnotes.en: that is, the doctrine of the law, which fed the carnal or little people with milk: but

headnotes.la: Ecclesiae doctores, qui fortem et validum verbi cibum manducant, et distribuunt. Unde Hebr. V
headnotes.en: the doctors of the Church, who eat and distribute the strong and solid food of the word. Whence Hebr. V

headnotes.la: …s haereticorum: qui circumferuntur omni vento doctrinae, inde etiam apostoli aliqui assumpti: ibi saepe Dominus docuit. Pertingit autem usque ad Sidonem, id est, usque ad gentes pervenit. Unde Isa. IX
headnotes.en: …ed about with every wind of doctrine, thence also were some of the apostles taken: there the Lord often taught. And he reaches as far as Sidon, that is, he comes as far as the Gentiles. Whence Isa. IX

headnotes.la: etc. Sidon, *venatio:* et ex eis locis sumpti sunt venatores, de quibus dicitur Jer. XVI
headnotes.en: …e Jordan of the Galilee of the Gentiles was heavily loaded"; the wording Migne prints is that of Mt 4:15.] Sidon, *hunting:* and out of those places were taken the hunters, of whom it is said Jer. XVI

headnotes.la: [n: (ISID.)] Christus ante et retro praeliabitur contra Antichristum: ante, occulto adventu humilitatis; post, manifestata gloria majestatis. Unde Moyses Deut. XXXIII
headnotes.en: [n: (ISID.)] Christ shall fight before and behind against Antichrist: before, by the hidden coming of his humility; after, by the manifested glory of his majesty. Whence Moses, Deut. XXXIII

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (ISID.)] Quidam doctorum hoc ad Hierusalem retulit, etc., *usque ad* tunc dividet escam, intelligens a spiritu litteram esse dividendam, quia
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (ISID.)] A certain one of the doctors referred this to Jerusalem, etc., *as far as* then shall he divide the food, understanding that the letter is to be divided from the spirit, because

headnotes.la: …uos de liberis et ancillis genuit, aequali honore filios et haeredes constituerit? quia sicut Christus omnibus qui per fidem corpori ejus conciliantur, pari honore et gloria coelestia praemia largitur
headnotes.en: … whom he begot of free women and of handmaids sons and heirs with equal honour? because, as Christ bestows heavenly rewards with like honour and glory upon all who are joined to his body through faith

headnotes.la: … qui formam servi induit, et pro libero et pro servo servivit, ut omnibus aequale donum largiatur. Quicunque enim fidem Domini promeretur, nullis maculis carnalis nativitatis offuscatur. Unde Joel. II
headnotes.en: …, and served both for the free man and for the servant, that he might bestow an equal gift upon all. For whosoever earns the faith of the Lord is darkened by no stains of carnal birth. Whence Joel. II

headnotes.la: …, sed populus multitudo est. Illi autem tam pauci non poterant populus dici. Intelligendum ergo hoc etiam de angelis dici, ad quorum societatem, de mundo transeuntes, apponuntur sancti. Unde Hebr. XII
headnotes.en: …ng so few, could not be called a people. It is to be understood therefore that this is said of the angels also, to whose fellowship the saints, passing out of the world, are gathered. Whence Hebr. XII

headnotes.la: …a dies jejuniorum sunt constituti, quibus Moyses, et Elias, et ipse Dominus jejunavit, et Ecclesia praecipuam observationem jejuniorum Quadragesimam vocat. Unde et apud Jonam de Ninivitis scriptum est
headnotes.en: …s of fastings appointed, on which Moses, and Elias, and the Lord himself fasted, and the Church calls the chief observance of fastings Lent. Whence also concerning the Ninivites it is written in Jonas

headnotes.la: …aginta enim dies post resurrectionem fuit Dominus cum discipulis suis intrans et exiens, manducans et bibens, qui dies laetitiae fuerunt. Nec septuaginta Interpretes errasse credendi sunt qui dixerunt
headnotes.en: … the resurrection the Lord was with his disciples, going in and going out, eating and drinking, and those were days of gladness. Nor are the seventy Interpreters to be believed to have erred, who said

headnotes.la: majore enim auctoritate praediti quam interpretum officium est, prophetico spiritu (quo etiam ore uno in suis interpretationibus, quod magnum miraculum fuit, consonuisse firmantur)
headnotes.en: … authority than the office of interpreters is, by the prophetic spirit (by which also they are affirmed to have agreed with one mouth in their interpretations, which was a great miracle) they set down
although they were not ignorant that

headnotes.la: in Hebraeo legerentur; ut in Christi clarificatione intelligerentur dissolvi et aboleri peccata,
headnotes.en: was read in the Hebrew; that in the glorification of Christ sins might be understood to be dissolved and abolished,

headnotes.la: [n: (STRAB.)] Ethnici novem diebus mortuos suos flebant. Unde et novendialis nona dies vocabatur, quando sepeliebantur. Dei cultores septem diebus exsequias celebrabant. Unde Eccli. XXII
headnotes.en: …The heathen bewailed their dead nine days. Whence also the ninth day was called the novendial, when they were buried. The worshippers of God celebrated the obsequies for seven days. Whence Eccli. XXII

headnotes.la: … requiem significat. Unde septima dies sabbatum, id est *requies* dicitur. Celebrant ergo septimam diem mortuorum, optantes illos cum Domino requiescere a laboribus praesentis vitae. Hinc ergo dicitur
headnotes.en: … is called the sabbath, that is, *rest*. They celebrate therefore the seventh day of the dead, wishing that they may rest with the Lord from the labours of the present life. Hence therefore it is said

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (AUG.)] Quod mandavit Joseph potentibus Aegypti, ut dicerent Pharaoni nomine ejus
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (AUG.)] As to what Joseph enjoined upon the great men of Egypt, that they should say to Pharao in his name

headnotes.la: …ni vitae reservatur. Siquidem in fide, spe et charitate custodita fuerit, per gratiam Christi pervenire merebitur ad speciem divinae contemplationis, cujus adoptio perfecta est laetitia; unde psal. XV
headnotes.en: …if it shall have been guarded in faith, hope and charity, it will deserve to come, by the grace of Christ, to the sight of the divine contemplation, whose adoption is perfect gladness; whence psal. XV
